recentItems.title: Cape Town hosts Energy Week: Ibra Ndiaye on new investments
recentItems.description:
Africa stands at a critical economic crossroads, with approximately 600 million people still without electricity the continent faces an urgent challenge of expanding energy access while transitioning towards cleaner, more sustainable energy sources.

This week, Cape Town hosts Energy Week, bringing the spotlight to key issues shaping the continent's energy future, including energy security, investment in renewable energy, and the role of emerging technologies such as green hydrogen and artificial intelligence (AI). 

But how does Africa balance its development needs with the global push for a greener economy, particularly while many countries still depend on fossil fuels?

To unpack these questions, we are joined by Ibra Ndiaye, an energy expert from Forvis Mazars.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Baphutheng Secondary School: 50 Limpopo learners' futures hangs in the balance
recentItems.description:
50 former learners from Limpopo are facing renewed uncertainty over their 2024 matric results. 

The Limpopo High Court ruled in their favour after their results in Business Studies and Economics were withheld over allegations of group copying. 

But the Department of Education is appealing against the ruling, potentially prolonging a fight that has already kept these learners waiting for almost two years. 

For more on this, we have invited one of the affected pupils who will remain anonymous and we are also joined Thato Gaffane from Section27. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Marking International Day of the Girl Child
recentItems.description:
October 11 marks the International Day of the Girl Child, a chance to celebrate girls' achievements and confront the barriers that can limit their opportunities.

The Department of Basic Education, Unilever through Dove, and the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) will tomorrow bring 240 learners, educators, partners and community stakeholders together in the North West. 

The event follows a week of learner dialogues and Dove Self-Esteem Project workshops in Potchefstroom schools, reaching 1,000 learners.

The focus is moving from awareness to action, helping girls build confidence, use their voices, make informed choices, and lead with purpose.

Joining us to discuss the initiative is Likho Bottoman, Director of Social Cohesion at the Department of Basic Education.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Asylum Seekers | IMC turns to ConCourt & High Court for guidance amid outrage & violent protests
recentItems.description:
The Inter-Ministerial Committee (IMC) on Migration will now turn to the Constitutional Court to seek a supervisory order that will guide its implementation of the apex court's ruling on fair access to the refugee system.

In addition, a parallel process will unfold at the Gauteng High Court, which is set—at the end of October—to establish legal certainty on how to approach asylum seekers who are detained and express an intention to apply: must they be released, or must the application process be facilitated from within the detention center?

This, as protests over undocumented immigration continue to grow in parts of the country.

SABC News senior reporter Canny Maphanga joins us for an update. 

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Mental Health Month | Breaking the cycle of violence via early emotional regulation
recentItems.description:
{WARNING: GRAPHIC CONTENT}

As South Africa grapples with a spate of murders over the past two months, questions are mounting about the roots of violent behaviour, and whether more can be done to prevent it.

As we mark Mental Health Awareness Month, we explore the link between childhood trauma, undiagnosed mental health conditions and the growing concern around gender-based violence.Could early intervention and emotional regulation help break the cycle of violence?

To unpack this, we're joined by Zonja Penzhorn, founder and CEO of Human Nature Africa, whose Plant Play research explores how emotional regulation can help prevent harmful behaviour.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Multi-million rand project collapses as contractors abandon site in Bez Valley
recentItems.description:
For two years, residents of Bez Valley and Bertrams, east of Johannesburg, have lived without consistent water and electricity. 

A multi-million rand project meant to fix leaking water and repair sewer pipes collapsed after three consecutive main contractors hired by Johannesburg Water abandoned the site - after also allegedly damaging electricity infrastructure.

Today, what remains is a maze of wide-open, hazardous trenches cutting through the community, while contractors point to non-payment by the City. 

SABC News reporter, Nomvuyo Ntanjana filed this report.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: LGE 2026 | Newly-formed MIV party on a door-to-door campaign
recentItems.description:
The Molemole Independent Voice (MIV) is a newly-formed party established in August 2026.

It started out as a community movement after residents of the Capricorn District Municipality, which include Blouberg, Polokwane and Molemole complained about poor service delivery.

As SABC News' Lutendo Bobodi  reports, the party plans to contest for 16 wards in Limpopo province.
